Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Second Quarter Fiscal 2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Second Quarter Fiscal 2025 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Lisa Wong, CTO; David Kim, Chief Revenue Officer; Emma Rodriguez, Chief Product Officer; and Jordan Lee, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for the second quarter of fiscal 2025. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: gross margin expansion, free cash flow generation, MRR growth trends, expansion revenue from existing customers, next quarter ARR guidance, sales efficiency improvements, and strengthening LTV/CAC ratios.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $105 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.5%, and operating income was $24 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $450 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $430 million to $450 million.

To provide more color on the key areas Sarah highlighted, let's start with gross margin performance, which continues to reflect the strong operating leverage inherent in our SaaS model. For Q2 fiscal 2025, we delivered a non-GAAP gross margin of 82.5%, up 130 basis points sequentially from 81.2% in the prior quarter and 270 basis points year-over-year from 79.8%. On a GAAP basis, gross margin was 81.1%, compared to 79.8% last quarter and 78.5% a year ago, primarily due to a $2.2 million stock-based compensation impact this quarter.

This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of gross margin improvement, underscoring the scalability of our cloud-native platform as we serve over 4,500 enterprise customers with our AI-powered collaboration and analytics suite, CloudForge Enterprise. Key drivers include infrastructure efficiencies, which accounted for about 80 basis points of the sequential expansion. We've optimized our multi-cloud footprint—primarily AWS and Google Cloud—through reserved instance commitments, spot instance utilization for non-critical workloads, and our proprietary auto-scaling orchestration layer. This reduced our effective cost of cloud compute by 18% quarter-over-quarter, even as we ramped usage to support 25% year-over-year ARR growth. Our dollar-based net expansion rate held steady at 118%, driving higher revenue per customer without proportional COGS increases. We're targeting sub-20% of revenue for hosting costs by fiscal 2025 end, benchmarking favorably against peers like Snowflake.

Product mix shift contributed around 50 basis points. Our high-margin AI modules—ForgeAI Insights and predictive analytics—now represent 32% of total ARR, up from 25% a year ago, as customers upgrade amid the generative AI wave. These modules boast gross margins north of 90%, far outpacing our legacy collaboration tools at around 78%. We expect this mix to improve to 40% of ARR by year-end fiscal 2025 with ForgeAI 2.0 and multimodal capabilities.

Regionally, our U.S. business—which is 65% of revenue—expanded to 84.2% gross margin, benefiting from mature scale and hyperscaler negotiations. EMEA, at 18% of revenue, improved to 80.1% from 77.5% year-over-year, driven by localized data sovereignty compliance reducing egress fees under GDPR. APAC remains at 76.8%, pressured by higher support costs in Japan and India, but AI-driven self-serve onboarding is targeting 80%+ by next quarter.

Customer support efficiencies offset $1.1 million in one-time data migration expenses from a large enterprise win. Our Net Promoter Score climbed to 68, enabling a 15% reduction in live support tickets via ForgeBot, our GenAI agent—now handling 45% of Tier 1 queries. As ACV scales from $150K to $220K for our top 20% cohort, support scales sublinearly.

Looking forward, we see sustained expansion to 83-84% non-GAAP gross margins in fiscal 2025, fueled by $250 million in R&D for edge computing and zero-ETL integrations. In a market squeezing SaaS multiples, our trajectory positions us for premium re-rating.

Next, on free cash flow, which highlights our asset-light SaaS model and operational efficiency focus. For the full fiscal year to date in 2025, we've generated strong free cash flow, building on $285 million for full fiscal 2024—a 52% year-over-year increase from $187 million in FY2023. This extends our streak of positive free cash flow for 11 consecutive quarters, even amid elevated interest rates and enterprise budget scrutiny.

Cash from operations was robust, with CapEx minimal at under 3% of revenue, tied to data center expansions for multi-tenant cloud infrastructure and AI tooling in ForgeAI. This allows nearly 94% conversion of operating cash flow to FCF, typical for mature SaaS like ServiceNow or Workday.

Primary driver—about 60% of uplift—is revenue growth and monetization efficiency. ARR grew 28% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, with NRR at 118% above industry benchmarks. Expansions accounted for 65% of new ARR, especially ForgeAI for devops and marketing, with land-and-expand deals scaling ACV rapidly.

Operating leverage contributed 25%, with GAAP operating margins at 22%, S&M down to 38% of revenue, CAC payback at 14 months, and LTV/CAC at 5.2x—top quartile per Bessemer. R&D in serverless cut infrastructure costs 20%.

Working capital optimization added 10%, with DSO at 52 days via automated invoicing, deferred revenue up 32% to $450 million.

Regionally, North America drove 75% at $214 million up 60%, EMEA 15% surging 75%, APAC 10% up 25% with new data centers.

For FY2025, expect $380-410 million FCF, 35-45% growth, with margins to 28%, funding repurchases and M&A.

Turning to MRR trends, our north star metric reflecting predictable revenue from the AI-powered DevOps platform. We ended Q2 FY2025 with $28.7 million in MRR, up 45% year-over-year from $19.8 million and 12% sequentially from $25.6 million.

New logo MRR was $4.2 million, up 30% quarter-over-quarter from 47 new customers, with ACV at $89K shifting to consumption-based pricing like Snowflake.

Expansion added $2.8 million, pushing NRR to 118% from 112%, driven by ForgeAI 2.0 launch with 65% adoption.

Retention: GDR 96%, annualized churn 4.2% down 80 basis points, contraction 1.8% via Expansion Playbook rescuing $1.1 million MRR.

U.S. 62% at $17.8 million up 48%, EMEA 28% growth to $8.0 million, APAC 12% at $3.4 million up 55%.

Expect Q3 MRR 42-45% YoY, sequential 11-13% with ForgeAI Enterprise.

Now, expansion revenue, core to our land-and-expand model. In the quarter, it reached $28.4 million, up 42% year-over-year and 11% sequentially, 28% of total revenue. DBNER at 124% above benchmarks.

Tier upgrades drove $12.7 million, ACV to $450K. AI Insights Engine $9.2 million with 41% penetration, Collaboration Hub $4.1 million, seat expansions $2.4 million.

North America 68% at $19.3 million up 38%, EMEA 52% to $5.6 million, APAC 65% to $4.2 million.

With 98% gross retention, expect Q4 DBNER 127%.

For next quarter ARR guidance, ending Q2 ARR was $485 million, up 29% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, NRR 118%, churn 4.5%.

Q3 guidance: $505 million to $515 million, 4-6% sequential, 31-34% YoY, on track for FY2025 $2.1 billion.

New logos $25-30 million from 450 customers, expansions $35-40 million DBNER 116-120%. AI Agent Builder 65% live.

Agentic Workflow Suite GA, platform modernization.

Regions: NA 5%, EMEA 7%, APAC high-teens.

Conservative amid macro, with Rule of 40 at 62.

On sales efficiency, sales cycle averaged 92 days for enterprise, down 15% QoQ and 28% YoY, top quartile.

Mid-market 65 days PLG, enterprise expansions 142 days. U.S. 85, EMEA 105, APAC 78.

AI sales stack with Outreach, Gong, self-serve demos cut 25 days.

Conversion overall 12.3% up 200 bps: MQL-SQL 32% +3 pts, SQL-opp 48% +2, opp-won 38% +4.

U.S. 14.5%, EMEA 9.8%. CAC payback 14 months, magic number 1.4.

Guide to 85 days, 30% new ARR self-serve.

Finally, LTV/CAC at 3.9x, up from 3.4x QoQ and 2.8x YoY, top quartile.

LTV $38,200 from $148K ARR/customer, 82% margin, 0.8% monthly churn. CAC $9,800 down 15%, S&M $6,100.

Cohorts Q1 2023 at 4.2x, APAC 3.1x improving. NA 4.5x, EMEA 3.6x, APAC 3.1x.

ForgeAI Predict boosts conversions 31%, self-serve 22% expansion. Target 5x by EOY.

These metrics position us strongly.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Wong for a technology update.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including Kubernetes-native migrations and 99.99% uptime SLAs.

And now Emma Rodriguez will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Emma Rodriguez:
Thank you, Lisa. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of ForgeAI Agent Builder. This new feature significantly improves workflow automation and productivity by up to 40% through autonomous process orchestration. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature, which aligns with our product strategy of AI everywhere.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Emma. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and a 35% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives, including ABM and intent data integrations.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

David Kim:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been transformative for our growth, contributing over 30% of new ARR this quarter through seamless upsells and new logos. We're seeing attach rates of 65% among eligible customers, particularly in enterprise accounts where it drives predictive analytics and automation. This has exceeded our initial expectations by 20%, as adoption accelerated faster than anticipated amid the agentic AI shift. Competitively, we're gaining share from legacy tools like ServiceNow and UiPath, thanks to our native multi-cloud integrations and lower TCO—our win rates against them are up 15%—while peers like Snowflake validate the consumption model we're pioneering.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Laura Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, and what are your expected ROI from these investments?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Laura. International expansion remains a priority, with APAC as a high-growth focus. We're investing in localized data centers in Tokyo and Singapore, partnering with Alibaba Cloud and Tencent for compliance. Key targets are Japan for manufacturing, India for fintech, and Australia for healthcare, where just-in-time AI workflows resonate. We expect ROI of 3x within two years, based on current pilots yielding 45% YoY growth and payback under 18 months, mirroring our EMEA ramp.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with JPMorgan.

Tom Rivera:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, and what's the impact of pricing changes on churn?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Tom. Churn management is proactive in this environment—we're at 4.2% annualized, elite levels, through predictive analytics flagging at-risk accounts early. NRR trended up to 118%, sixth straight quarter of expansion from cohort maturity and AI upsells. Retention strategies include the Expansion Playbook, ForgeBot for self-serve support boosting NPS to 68, and CSM pods for top accounts. Recent pricing changes—dynamic tiers for AI modules—have actually reduced churn by 80 basis points, as value perception offsets with 15% ASP uplift and multi-year commitments now at 85% of ACV.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
